summary: Read-only review complete; two authorization gaps remain. No edits, builds, tests, or network access. Requested password-vendure.ts is absent; reviewed password.ts and password-vendure.test.ts.

findings.title: Admin password change can consume invalidated step-up authority
findings.detail: The row leaves changeAdminPassword unchanged. routes/admin-security.ts:174 checks only the cached principal's step-up before password verification and hashing; auth/admin-session.ts:94-110 subsequently checks only password-hash equality and session existence/absolute expiry. A password-change request paused after that admission can resume after deletion of its authorizing passkey or a TOTP cycle clears step-up on the retained session, then change the password and revoke other sessions. Trigger-driven clearing does not revoke the already-cached authorization.
findings.fix: | Admin password change (`admin-security.ts` → `admin-session.ts`) | Cached `requireStepUp` → password verification and hashing → `admin_user` `FOR UPDATE` → kept session `FOR UPDATE`; the mutation currently checks only the password hash and session absolute expiry | **restructured**: before password verification, read the owner's `security_epoch`, `password_hash` and stored TOTP version together with the calling session's `step_up_at` and `step_up_epoch`, and require a fresh step-up for that snapshot. Carry these captured values into `changeAdminPassword`. In its mutation transaction: `admin_user` `FOR UPDATE` → require the captured epoch and credential snapshot to match → calling session `FOR UPDATE` → revalidate owner, absolute expiry, idle expiry, step-up freshness, `step_up_epoch = security_epoch`, and equality of both step-up fields to the captured proof. Reject changed proof with 409 `CREDENTIAL_CHANGED` before any password update or revocation. Only then update the password and revoke other sessions atomically; the trigger clears step-ups. Add deterministic real-route tests that pause password change after verification, delete the authorizing passkey or disable and re-enable TOTP while retaining the calling session, then resume and prove the password and remaining sessions are unchanged. Cover both lock interleavings without retries or sleeps. |

findings.title: Factor mutations still omit the captured security epoch
findings.detail: The replacement fixes replay-lock ordering but leaves mutateAdminSecondFactor's snapshot check at passwordHash plus totpVersion (auth/admin-staff.ts:64-73). Recovery-code regeneration verifies its factor outside that transaction (routes/admin-security.ts:146-152). On supported plaintext-TOTP installations, a pending regeneration can survive disable/re-enable with the same secret and retained session, then replace recovery codes using proof from the previous epoch. Enrollment likewise cannot distinguish NULL before an enable/disable cycle from NULL afterward. Adding epoch checks only to native login and step-up leaves these credential mutations outside the promised invariant.
findings.fix: | Admin factor mutations and standalone TOTP verification (`admin-staff.ts`, `second-factor.ts`) | Factor mutation: credential advisory → admin `FOR UPDATE` → session `FOR UPDATE` → replay advisory; standalone TOTP verification: replay advisory → replay-row insert → implicit admin FK `KEY SHARE` | **restructured**: capture `security_epoch`, `password_hash` and the stored TOTP version together before password or factor verification for enable, disable and recovery-code regeneration. Pass the captured epoch explicitly through every `mutateAdminSecondFactor` caller, including the enable caller's explicit argument object. After the credential advisory lock and admin `FOR UPDATE`, require the captured epoch and both credential snapshots to equal the locked row before locking the calling session or performing any mutation; otherwise return 409 `CREDENTIAL_CHANGED`. Retain session owner, expiry and idle revalidation. Standalone `verifyTotpOnce` acquires the existing admin row `FOR SHARE` in its own transaction before acquiring the `totp-step` advisory lock or touching replay rows, and refuses a missing owner. Transactional factor verification uses the caller's already-held admin `FOR UPDATE` lock before the replay advisory lock; never acquire the owner after the replay advisory lock. Keep standalone verification committed before subsequent mutation transactions, which must re-check their captured epochs and credential snapshots. Add the TOTP invariant check (passkeys exist → 409 `PASSKEYS_ENROLLED` on disable); the trigger performs epoch/step-up invalidation. Add deterministic real-route races between TOTP disable and standalone verification through login, native step-up, enrolment and recovery-code regeneration. Also pause regeneration after successful factor verification, disable and re-enable the same plaintext secret using the retained calling session, then prove the pending regeneration cannot replace recovery codes; pause enrolment across a NULL → secret → NULL cycle and prove it cannot install its previously verified secret. Cover both lock interleavings without retries or sleeps. |
